CANOPTICON·The standing record
Record Investigations Method / ask the record
How this works

What Canopticon actually is.

Not a separate doc that goes stale in a repo nobody opens — this page. /method explains why a claim here can be trusted. This explains the shape of the whole thing: what content types exist and why, what's really built versus still open, and what runs on its own between visits.

1396subjects on file
61source documents
4402documented facts
4437verbatim quotes
1signed investigations
48themes surfaced

The one-sentence version

Canopticon reads research documents into a typed graph of facts, grows a citable public record from that graph automatically, drafts signed readings on top of it, and the operator approves what publishes. The operator approves; the operator never authors. Nobody writes a page by hand — pages grow as documents are read, and the same graph fans out into every format below without being regenerated from scratch each time.

The content types

Everything public is one of five kinds of thing. This is the part that's easiest to lose track of session to session — so it's written down here, not just in a design doc.

Records

One page per person, company, event, or theme — /s/:slug. Two modes: neutral (the facts and their receipts, disputed material shown gray) and signed (the operator's reading — the same facts, re-sequenced under a thesis, with a mandatory box of what complicates it). This is the spine everything else hangs off.

Arrangements — twelve ways to view the same facts

Every arrangement is both a section embedded inside a Record and its own standalone, independently-citable page with its own schema.org markup. That's deliberate, for GEO: a fine-grained URL with specific structured data out-cites a subject page that merely has the same content as one section among several. They're not meant to be found by clicking through site nav — they're meant to be found by search engines and AI answer engines, and reached from the Record they belong to.

Investigations — the signed layer

A signed reading wears one of seven intents as a badge — its epistemic stance, not a nav category:

Investigationan open, skeptical probe — often doesn't conclude
Argumenta closed case
Patterna recurring structure across instances
Hypothesisa candidate explanation, held provisionally
Assessmenta judgment with a stated confidence band
Critiqueattacks one specific claim
Explanationconnects the dots, low advocacy
Faces — one reading, many formats

Every signed reading renders as tabs: Thread and Card are pure template + query — no LLM call, instant, straight from the thesis and the highest-ranked stored quotes. Video script and chapter outline need real argumentative sequencing, so those get one LLM pass at the moment you sign, persisted from then on — every later view is still instant. Nothing here is "generating your script" on click; either it's already rendered, or it was rendered once and stored.

Studio — the production room

Not where you generate content — faces already did that. Studio turns a rendered face into a downloadable asset. Shipped: card / thread / carousel → PNG, newsletter → email-safe HTML, long-form → Markdown. Not yet: voice recording + cloning, video assembly (Flux stills → Wan animation → MiniMax voiceover), a documentary stage, a two-voice podcast stage, and a distribution log — all real, all deliberately deferred until there's a working voice profile to build them on.

The firewall, briefly

A fact only exists on this site if it's a word-for-word quote from a document actually stored here, checked mechanically. An attributed claim (someone said X) is never silently stated as settled fact. This is the one rule everything else is built around — see /method for the full mechanics.

The standing newsroom

The system doesn't just wait for uploads. Several things run on their own, on a schedule, without you:

The sweep

Every few hours, one pass picks the single most worth-pursuing thin subject and runs a real search → fetch → verbatim-extract cycle on it — the same pipeline as the "Expand this file" button, just fired automatically. Priority goes to beats first, then subjects the graph already talks about a lot but hasn't verified yet (edge_degree), with an extra boost for subjects a surfaced contradiction or cross-document connection is specifically about.

Beats

Standing coverage areas you name — a person, an institution, a topic you want watched continuously, not just filled in once. A due beat gets first refusal on the sweep's one slot. Managed via /v1/admin/beats right now (no UI form yet).

Deep research

After a beat's sweep banks new sources, a separate pass writes a synthesized research brief from them — the "free-ish" equivalent of the Research toggle you'd otherwise run by hand — and that brief goes through the exact same verbatim extraction as anything you upload.

The settle pipeline

After documents come in, six steps run in the background to turn raw extraction into a usable record: entity resolution, event dedup, scoring contested evidence, surfacing themes and cross-document patterns, seeding pages, and drafting signed readings. One step runs per tick — chaining them all at once is exactly what silently broke this for a while; splitting it up is what fixed it.

The homepage's "Today, unattended" line is the honest status check: how many sweeps ran, sources banked, readings drafted, and duplicates merged today, so you're never left wondering if any of this is actually running.

What you can do

Sign a reading

A drafted reading waits under "Awaiting your signature" until you read it and sign or discard it. The system writes; you're the only one who publishes.

Expand a thin file

On any subject page, "Expand this file" fires the same search+fetch+extract cycle the sweep uses, right now, for that one subject.

Research a question

On a search that comes up empty, or on an open thread / finding with nowhere to click yet, "Research this" fires the same pipeline keyed to that exact question.

Bulk-expand the thinnest 3

One button on the homepage's status line, for when you want to nudge several gaps at once instead of waiting for the sweep's one-at-a-time cadence.

What's real vs. still open

Said plainly, so it can be checked rather than assumed:

Shipped and live
  • All twelve arrangement URLs (one, Comparison, is scaffold-only — see the table above)
  • Template+query faces (thread, card, carousel) — instant, no LLM
  • LLM-seasoned faces (video script, chapter outline) — one pass on signing, then instant
  • Semantic search (/search)
  • The citation tracker (/citations, operator-only)
  • Record-building on click — search → fetch → extract, same pipeline the sweep uses
  • Studio Stage A — card/thread/carousel → PNG, newsletter, long-form export
Deliberately not built yet
  • Comparison arrangement's real query logic (renders its honest empty state today)
  • Studio Stage B–F — voice recording/cloning, video assembly, documentary, podcast, distribution log
  • Concurrent extraction (Cloudflare Queues + Durable Objects) — parked on account setup
  • The frontier-model tier — one line in the router, saved for near launch
  • "Ask the corpus" as a conversational surface — shape not yet decided

What it costs

None of the automatic parts are free: Brave Search calls and Workers AI inference both cost real money, metered. Everything above is deliberately capped — one subject per sweep tick, one candidate per settle step, bulk-expand capped at 3 — on purpose, so unattended operation stays bounded rather than open-ended.

✓

Every documented fact on this site is backed by a word-for-word quote from a source document we have stored — checked by machine, not vouched for. Disputed claims are shown as disputed. Claims that fail verification are removed, and we say so. How verification works →
